title: Parameter-cover norms, integral critical values and the whole polynomial output class

retained_primary_inputs.title: Quantitative properties of the non-properness set of a polynomial map
retained_primary_inputs.role: Explicit proof input: Definition 2.1, Proposition 2.2, Definition 2.3, and Theorem 3.2. For a generically finite polynomial map from complex affine space, its nonproperness set is covered by nonconstant polynomial images of A1. Only this qualitative conclusion is used, not the degree bound.

Section 58.13, inertia definition, Lemmas 58.13.1-2, Example 58.13.3 and Lemma 58.13.4: inertia kernels describe the unramified quotient; for a regular base codimension-one inertia suffices by purity.
Retained purity for the finite normal quotient cover on the smooth regular target D times A^(n-1), after every actual divisorial inertia group is killed.

Retained Milne v2.21 Theorem 3.4 full faithfulness, already imported in HC4MYIJ1: an algebraic section restriction of a finite etale cover on D times affine space and its pullback have a topological isomorphism which is algebraic. Both covers already exist algebraically; essential surjectivity is not used.
retained_primary_inputs.portions_inspected_this_turn: Entire printed page 28 via the accessible primary PDF, including the theorem, its hypotheses and the following fundamental-group identification; also printed pages 27 and 29 for context.

retained_primary_inputs.role: Retained Theorem 1(i) to (iii) and the HC4MYHX0 field argument: every Keller component f_1 gives a relatively algebraically closed C(f_1), preserving every finite parameter-cover group. No new statement from this source is imported.
Proposition 41.19.7: normality is preserved by an etale local ring map. Used after etale Keller base change of a normal monogenic cover.

newly_cached_primary_inputs.role: Smoothness is stable under composition and base change, Lemmas 29.35.4-5 in the inspected current page; local standard-smooth descriptions justify the nowhere-critical polynomial parameter morphism. This structural input makes the actual source base change smooth over C.

Lemmas 33.25.3-4 and 33.25.8: smooth finite-type schemes over C are regular and normal, and regular finite-type complex curves are smooth. Used for the finite normal parameter curve and its smooth source base change.

Lemma 31.18.6: the finite locally free norm is the determinant of multiplication and commutes with base change. The proof note repeats this determinant construction and the unit implication in its finite-free situation; this is an explicit primary reference for the convention.

newly_cached_primary_inputs.title: Another elementary proof of Luroth's theorem
newly_cached_primary_inputs.author: Michael Bensimhoun
newly_cached_primary_inputs.version: Jerusalem, 10 May 2004; retained two-page primary paper
newly_cached_primary_inputs.role: Explicit ordinary one-variable Luroth import: for any field k, a nonconstant intermediate field between k and k(z) is k(S) for rational S. Both pages of the primary theorem and proof were inspected. Only the theorem is imported; the unique-pole polynomial refinement is proved directly. No Ritt classification, indecomposable-group classification or multivariate Luroth theorem is imported.
